gen-gf-tektur-gf-epunda-sans: Tektur draws every stroke like bent wire, ruler-straight and uniform, with outsized lowercase and curves that gape open at the ends. Epunda Sans, a sans-serif with generous counters, keeps a long read light.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-farro: Tektur brings wiry strokes and oversized lowercase, every curve left open at its terminal. And Farro, a sans with short ascenders and no stroke contrast at all, is the approachable half of the pair.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-fragment-mono: Wire-bent and a bit futuristic, Tektur leads with open curves and outsized lowercase. Fragment Mono follows in monospace, its letters lined up like nails on a ruler, and that rigid order is the pair's best trick.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-geist-mono: Geist Mono lays down fixed-width, code-style monospace with high-rising lowercase and generous gaps between letters, under Tektur's wiry display heading. Longer text moves in a steady, structured tick.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-genos: Genos packs its sans-serif glyphs so tightly the edges almost touch, with a high midline and no clogged bowls. But Tektur's stout, pipe-cleaner strokes look far more playful beside that compact, contemporary text.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-geom: Geom has a lofty lowercase band. Tektur above it is made of one unbroken, wire-like line weight, while Geom's plain sans text stays approachable, and that mix of tubing and polish is the pair's best quality.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-hammersmith-one: Outsized lowercase and open curves make Tektur look like bent pipe cleaner, instantly distinctive. And Hammersmith One, a sans with rounded, cord-like strokes and capitals barely above lowercase, keeps longer text smooth.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-inder: Expressive Tektur has tubular, wire-like letterforms. Inder, a plain sans with little height difference between its capitals and lowercase, sits underneath as a clean, professional counterweight that lets the heading do the talking.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-jaldi: Tektur holds a single monoline weight with generous openings, giving the heading a wire-bent, expressive look. Jaldi, a plain sans with a tall x-height, fills in beneath it.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-kdam-thmor-pro: Tektur has curves as thick as its stems. Kdam Thmor Pro, a sans with bowls that fill the line, makes a longer read feel modern and dense, a bit more tightly packed than the heading.
